content.comment_body: Hello, I'm developing software using S7.net and have established a successful connection. I'm working with VM mapping and have set VB0 (4 bytes for a counter). However, when I use S7.net and enter the address VB0, I get an error indicating that 'V' is not a valid address. Why does this happen? This address was defined in [product_name] V[version_no].
The VM-Memory of the [product_name] can be accessed as a DB. Try using DB1.DBD0 instead.

analysis.insight_summary: A user experienced an address mapping error when trying to access VM memory (VB0) of a [product_name] device using the S7.net library in C#. The address format specified in [product_name] V[version_no] was not recognized by S7.net, causing confusion and a validity error. Another user recommended using DB addressing (DB1.DBD0) to fix the issue, highlighting a difference in how memory addresses are handled between the [company_name] software and third-party libraries.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipates that the memory address format (VB0), configured in [product_name] V[version_no], should be directly compatible and usable with the S7.net library for smooth data communication.
